title: Capacity Cost Pivot — Q3 Budget Playbook
content:
Purpose:
Quick playbook + working-sheet for Q3 budgeting where we need to pivot capacity and price levers to protect runway while preserving go-to-market momentum. This is intentionally a concise, action-oriented sheet for finance + ops + product to iterate on scenarios and commit to owners.

High-level summary (single-line):
We run three scenarios (Hold, Tilt, Throttle) that trade headcount hiring, dedicated GPU commit levels, and a shallow price adjustment on high-consumption routes. Goal: retain ~85% of revenue growth potential while reducing incremental monthly burn by ~22% in the first 90 days.

Key assumptions (working):
- ARR baseline (end of Q2 run-rate): $115M annualized (rolling last-12 tokens).
- Current monthly burn (net of revenue): $5.2M.
- GPU commit and spot mix: 55% committed, 45% spot.
- Median request token length and payload unchanged in short term.
- Elasticity: conservative demand response of 2% revenue drop per 1% price increase on >1M token customers; higher sensitivity on price-sensitive web tier.
- Hiring lead time: 8–10 weeks for senior infra/serving hires; 4–6 weeks for junior roles via contractors.

Scenario overview:
1) Hold (baseline) — minimal pricing changes, pruning non-critical hires, small reserve rebalancing.
   - Headcount: freeze non-critical roles, continue critical infra hires (net +6 hires this quarter).
   - Capacity: maintain current committed GPU mix, reduce spot budget by 10%.
   - Expected short-term burn change: -6% (~$312k/mo).
   - Revenue impact: ~ -1.5% (estimated).

2) Tilt (preferred pivot) — targeted price tier bump for high-consumption routes + temporary hiring pause for some product roles.
   - Headcount: pause 40% of product hiring pipeline, continue SRE and serving-critical hires (net +2 hires).
   - Pricing: +5% on enterprise burst plans and new commit SKU; grandfather existing active committed customers for 90 days.
   - Capacity: shift 15% of committed reserve to short-term burst pool, reduce spot run by 25%.
   - Expected short-term burn change: -22% (~$1.14M/mo).
   - Revenue impact: modeled -3% in Q3 (with partial offset via billing collection push).

3) Throttle (defensive) — aggressive cost reduction and slower growth posture.
   - Headcount: hiring freeze except immediate critical SRE/ops hires (net -4 hires via offer pauses / contractor conversion).
   - Pricing: +10% on top-tier metered routes and additional tiering for ultra-high throughput customers; introduce temporary usage floor on new free-tier signups.
   - Capacity: reduce committed GPU renewals where contract >90 days out, aggressively lower spot spend by 50%, shut down non-prod reserved pools for 30 days.
   - Expected short-term burn change: -34% (~$1.78M/mo).
   - Revenue impact: modeled -6–9% in Q3 depending on customer churn.

Headcount snapshot (working table — rows):
Role bucket | Current FTE | Q3 plan delta | Hiring timeline | Notes
Engineering (serving/runtime) | 38 | +2 | 8w | prioritize kernel/quant work
SRE/Infra | 22 | +1 | 6w | capacity automation
Product (hosted/api, console) | 28 | -4 (pause) | paused | delay non-critical features
Sales & CS | 46 | 0 | ongoing | focus on collections & upsell
Finance & Ops | 12 | +1 (contractor) | 4w | billing/collections support
Total | 146 | -? (net scenarios vary) | | 

Pricing sensitivity quick-matrix (text table):
Change | Expected demand delta | ARR impact (annualized) | Impact on short-term burn
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
+2% price on high-consumption routes | -1% demand | +(2.3%)* ARR on route segment | small positive (offsets cost)
+5% targeted enterprise bump | -2.8% demand | +1.7% ARR overall | meaningful positive, low churn risk with grandfathering
+10% top-tier | -6% demand | -2.2% ARR overall | may increase churn, risk to net retention
Introduce commit-only discount removal (remove 10% off new commits) | -0.5% new commit velocity | negligible immediate ARR change | reduces long-run discount dilutive effect

Sensitivity notes:
- Price sensitivity is non-linear across segments; enterprise direct-contract customers are least price elastic in short window when given clear migration path. Consumer/web tier is most elastic.
- Our billing cadence (net 30 / 45) amplifies revenue realization delays; immediate burn relief from price changes is limited unless combined with capacity reductions.

Run-rate impact estimator (text):
- To achieve ~20% burn reduction over 90 days, recommended mix = Tilt scenario: a 5% targeted price increase on high-consumption routes + pause 40% of product hires + reduce spot spend by 25%.
- This combination avoids deep churn and preserves runway extension of ~4 months vs Hold.

Action items (owners and due dates):
1) Finalize list of "high-consumption routes" and affected SKUs — Marcus Holt — due 2026-08-18.
2) Draft customer communication play for targeted enterprise bump + grandfather rules — Linda Yang + GTM — due 2026-08-22.
3) Implement spot budget throttle plan and identify non-prod pools to pause — Owen Park (Infra) — due 2026-08-20.
4) Freeze criteria doc for product hires and candidate outreach plan for critical roles — Priya Nair + Eng hiring partners — due 2026-08-16.
5) Update forecast model with scenario toggles and run sensitivity Monte Carlo (5k sims, varying churn & elasticity) — Finance analytics — due 2026-08-26.

Open questions / tradeoffs (notes to reviewers):
- How do we handle customers on committed contracts that cross quarters? Do we grandfather full term or phase pricing changes? (legal/GTM tradeoff).
- Should we offer targeted credits for high-value customers who are likely to churn from price moves? Balance between retention vs signaling price softness.
- Operational complexity: can infra execute 25% spot reduction while maintaining latency SLOs for peak hours? Need SRE confirmation.

Quick checklist before leadership review:
- [ ] Attach detailed model (sheet) with scenario toggles and baseline assumptions (separate model file id: CON-48291).
- [ ] Finance runs Monte Carlo and attaches 90/10 downside outputs.
- [ ] Legal sign-off on grandfathering approach.
- [ ] GTM draft customer comms + support playbook.

Notes / scratchpad (raw):
- If we increase enterprise tier price by 5% but include a 3-month committed credits match for high-volume customers we could preserve ~75% of revenue while still raising realized unit economics — test with top 15 accounts first.
- Temporary non-prod reserve shutdown should be scheduled during maintenance windows; expect ~48–72h of catch-up risk for experiments but low business impact.

Next steps:
- Incorporate feedback from infra and GTM, finalize recommendation by 2026-08-30 for Exec review on 2026-09-02.

Version history / notes: 
- 2026-08-12 initial draft (Priya)
- 2026-08-15 added infra input (Owen)
- 2026-08-18 GTM sketch added (Linda)
- 2026-09-07 Monte Carlo placeholders added and moved to in_review

Bottom line: Tilt scenario (targeted price bump + focused headcount pause + moderate capacity rebalancing) is recommended as the first-line pivot to protect runway while keeping product momentum. This sheet is a working artifact — update numbers in the linked model before leadership sign-off.
